title: fix(gateway): avoid main-thread compile cache flush stalls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node compile-cache persistence synchronously blocks the Gateway main thread. The earlier startup flush in #171298 moved this cost before readiness; the compilecache2 experiment measured a 3.8-second cold main-thread flush. Disable caching on the Gateway main thread while retaining the existing build-scoped cache owner for workers and their existing flush boundaries.

## User Impact

Ordinary Gateway launches no longer pause the main event loop to persist Node bytecode. Worker caching remains enabled, preserving its startup benefit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher, compiled entry, and direct CLI entry pass the Gateway role to the shared owner. An inherited active cache uses the existing respawn handoff marker to start Node uncached, then restores worker caching. No new environment flag. Remove the two Gateway flush calls. Short-lived CLI commands, explicit prewarming, and caller-authored NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE retain their existing policies. Node permission mode retains an already-active caller cache because it may forbid process replacement; optional caching must not prevent startup.

## Scope and measurements

T1 compile-cache owner SQL calls: **0 → 0**. This change adds or removes no database statements or requests; no SQL saving is claimed. No schema, SDK, or database dialect changes.

| Metric | Early-flush baseline cold / warm | Candidate cold / warm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Boot → client ready | 16.158 / 14.644 s | 14.516 / 11.709 s |
| Main CPU near ready | 9.839–9.878 / 5.714–5.867 s | 5.570–5.760 / 5.589–5.819 s |
| Longest main timer lag | 3.538 / 1.350 s | 1.319 / 1.188 s |
| Longest main-thread cache flush | 3.455 / 0.005 s | 0 / 0 s |
| Shutdown | 0.383 / 0.285 s | 0.357 / 2.044 s |

Exactly four runs passed the shared 13-turn workload, alternating baseline/candidate cold then warm, on Node 24.21.0. Base 516eec6; measured candidate 13534272. Final head 74414fd6 only adds Windows platform guards and test corrections, preserving the measured macOS path. Warm CPU passes the 15% gate: the nearby checkpoint improves 2.18%; even candidate's upper bound against baseline's lower bound is only +1.84%. Candidate main cache enable/flush calls are 0/0; every run retains two cached workers and 48 worker flush calls.

These are observations on a shared 32-core host (one-minute load 22.86–41.94), not isolated latency claims. CPU bounds straddle readiness; timer lag includes scheduling delay and is not one continuously executing callback. Warm shutdown increased by 1.759 s: logs show overlapping memory-preparation/plugin-services cleanup taking 1.611/1.579 s, with no main cache flush or sampled shutdown lag above 50 ms. The logs do not establish why those steps took longer.

For historical context, compilecache2's main-only-disable experiment measured cold/warm ready 18.051/17.444 s, main CPU 9.199–9.213/7.594–7.617 s, zero main flushes, and shutdown 2.698/1.770 s. Its early-flush cold row had ready 28.594 s and a 3.780 s main flush. Those runs used another source revision; this is a behavior comparison, not a cross-revision speedup claim.

## Removed work and accepted edge cases

- Remove the main-thread startup/post-ready flush: the uncached main thread has no bytecode to persist.
- Remove the main-thread handler-prewarm flush: workers continue flushing their own isolate caches.
- No SQL authority, integrity, or security checks are removed. Disposable cache persistence remains best-effort.

## Evidence

- Focused tests pass: all 27 entry-owner cases across the initial run and five corrected Vitest-worker expectations; all eight subprocess cache-base cases across the initial run and one corrected empty-environment expectation. These cover uncached Gateway main, cached workers, inherited cache respawn, explicit disable, CLI policy, and uncached process exit.
- Codex autoreview: two rounds complete. Fixed the permission-mode startup regression found in round one; final round found no actionable P0/P1 defects.
- Fixed the additional automated-review P1: Node exposes unsupported `execve` on Windows, so all three entry points retain the existing child bridge there. The new launcher regression fails before the guard and passes afterward (417 ms). The POSIX lifecycle test now verifies preserved supervisor PID and signal propagation (3.285 s); both focused cases pass, with 80.43 s total runner time dominated by tooling transforms.
- Changed-file formatting and diff check pass. The local type-aware lint diagnostic in `node-compile-cache.d.mts` (`typescript/no-redundant-type-constituents` for `NodeJS.ProcessEnv`) was reproduced on baseline 516eec6. Final-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38467911867) completed successfully, including tests and static gates.
- The required combined CI/security gate is green. Its first security-workflow attempt exhausted retries while reading GitHub’s CI job list (30-second API timeouts); rerunning only that diagnosed infrastructure failure succeeded. No product tests were rerun for it.
- [Published-driver × final candidate update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38468038386/job/115547656010) passed once on exact head 74414fd6. Published driver `2026.10.3`; running candidate build identity matches the package. Stop → ready: **91.469 s**, from Gateway SIGTERM at 21:29:43.161Z to readiness at 21:31:14.630Z. Updater exit 0, recorded update succeeded, readiness HTTP 200. The cell also verifies managed-PID replacement, durable session survival, incognito cleanup, and orphan sidecar preservation.
- The first CI attempt exposed a stale POSIX child-PID expectation, fixed above. An obsolete update workflow was canceled before its update cell started; the final-head cell runs once. The broader main-tier update dispatch also exposes unrelated missing-`rg` PR-tooling fixtures and a Signal approval assertion matching [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38463809799/job/115525900711) exactly (`signal-approval-forwarding.integration.test.ts:118`). The obsolete dispatch also had an inherited storage-location authority-loss failure. These do not occur in the successful final-head ordinary PR CI run.
- LOC: 128 additions / 36 deletions across 11 files (including tests and documentation).
